en: The Jātaka:
The Fifth Chapter,
the Section on the Jeweled Earrings (Maṇikuṇḍalavagga)
6. The Koraṇḍiya Jātaka “Alone in a mountain cave in the forest,
you repeatedly pick up stones and hurl them down;”
“Koraṇḍiya, why are you so eager again and again?
What is it that you desire?
“I am indeed seeking this one who dwells by the ocean.”
"I shall make it level as if with my own hand;
having scattered the plateaus and the mountains,
I shall therefore cast this rock into the cleft."
“No single man is able to level this earth with his hands;
I think that only this cave can be conquered.”
“Koraṇḍiya, you have laughed at the world of the living. “If I am not able,
alone among men, to make the bearer of beings equal to myself;”
"In this very way, Brahmā, you will not lead these humans of various views to me.
"In brief, sir, for my sake..."
"Koraṇḍiyā, it is thus he has declared:
'Just as it is impossible for a person to make the earth level,
so too are human beings.'"
The Koraṇḍiya Jātaka, the sixth.
